messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [SEV-2] Elevated tail latency + 5xx spike for tenant edgewave in dedicated-pool-7 (vpc). Alerts: p99 latency 2.1s -> 6.8s, 5xx rate 0.9% -> 6.4%. Escalation to on-call (meera) at 10:02 UTC.
meera: taking pager, oncall here. pinging eng-runtime and customer success. started triage.
alex: saw the same in dashboards — queue depth for edgewave sched queue jumped, lots of large requests with long seqs. KV cache hit dropped too.
meera: ok quick plan: 1) isolate tenant to its bespoke queue policy (no cross-tenant coalesce), 2) reduce max_batch_tokens for that tenant to limit single-request amplification, 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant for that tenant for ~15m. execute order?
sam: +1. I can apply the scheduler knob change. will run as dry-run first to verify route.
jordan: adding context — edgewave has a long-running pipeline that saw a sudden increase in long-context summarize jobs (avg tokens/request ~ 18k). Their requests are single-shot large sequences, so batching is starving short requests.
meera: can we set max_batch_tokens=2048 for the tenant and lower per-slot batch_size? what are current values?
alex: current tenant override is max_batch_tokens=8192, max_batch_items=8. global defaults are 4096/16.
sam: applying patch now:
```bash
# reduce tokens per batch and force immediate flush for small requests
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant edgewave --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=2048 --set scheduler.max_batch_items=4 --reason "emergency oncall mitigation"
```
sam: patch applied, rolling through pool nodes in dedicated-pool-7. watching telemetry.
ops-bot: deploy started: change-id=chg-7821 by sam. nodes affected: 12/12.
devon: I configured a temporary routing rule to prefer model=curie-quantized for edgewave if latency > 1.5s. That reduces per-token cost but helps keep tail down.
meera: good. slack customer success to let edgewave support know we're doing mitigation. jordan, can you check backlog queue size and token-based queue time?
jordan: backlog tokens peaked at ~1.2M tokens in queue. avg headroom per GPU dropped to 6%. after knob change backlog tokens down to ~420k in 3 minutes.
alex: 5xx rate dropped from 6.4% -> 1.7% within 4m of changes. p99 down to 2.3s then trending.
meera: nice. keep observation window 15m. document actions and metrics for handoff.
sam: leaving watches for 20m and will set rollback if errors creep back.
incident-bot: NOTE: customer_edgewave_support contact=on-call-cs@edgewave.com notified at 10:08 UTC by meera.
meera: @devon can you keep the fallback model in place for 30m? if stable, we'll extend to 2h and schedule a follow-up with eng-runtime and CS.
devon: yep left in place. routing rule id=rte-559 active.
jordan: running a quick sim of potential secondary mitigation: apply kv-cache prefix warming for recent user flows — can cut cold cache misses contributing to latency. need ops approval to write small cache preloads.
meera: do it if low-risk. coordinate with sam.
sam: started cache preload for last-24h prefixes for edgewave. small sized (5k prefixes) to warm hot paths. logs: preload job job-331 enqueued.
ops-bot: job-331 started on pool nodes.
alex: telemetry update at +12m: p99 latency 1.1s, 5xx 0.4%, average throughput stable. Queue depth low.
meera: sounds good. preparing customer-facing incident note. key points: cause = sudden spike in long-context requests from edgewave leading to oversized batches and kv-cache churn; mitigation = reduced tenant max_batch_tokens & max_batch_items, routing fallback to smaller model, cache warming. no data exfiltration.
sam: creating internal playbook entry: command used and rollback steps. rollback: 
```bash
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant edgewave --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=8192 --set scheduler.max_batch_items=8 --reason "rollback after incident if needed"
redwoodctl routing disable --id rte-559
```
meera: handoff time in 20m to daytime oncall (alex). leaving notes here. if anything regresses ping me.
alex: acknowledged. I'll own post-mortem and customer follow-up scheduling.
incident-bot: Pager cleared at 10:24 UTC by meera. Incident state -> mitigated.
meera: quick runbook action items for post-mortem: 1) add an automated tenant-level long-context guard that alerts before queue tokens > 500k; 2) consider a soft per-request token limit or upstream validation for VPC tenants; 3) doc the scheduler knob effects on tail latency for dedicated pools.
jordan: I'll take item 1 and run a prototype alert.
meera: thanks all. closing thread after handoff notes written.
